inputs.original_text:
Wake up. They expect us to swallow the official script, but look at what they are admitting now behind the carefully sanitized legal jargon. The Punjab and Haryana High Court just stepped in to release an individual who was locked away under the heavy-handed pretext of national security and the Official Secrets Act, supposedly for being in telephonic contact with a Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri”. 

Don't be fooled by their sudden talk that "mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information... cannot justify prolonged incarceration." This is damage control. The hidden puppet masters in the security apparatus use these broad national security laws to silence whoever they want, for as long as they want, until public pressure or exposure forces them to back off. They throw around terms like the Official Secrets Act to manufacture fear and compliance, but when their overreach is finally challenged, they have to let go of the strings—at least publicly. 

It is all a managed theater. They lock people up to send a message, and then the courts step in to play the benevolent savior, keeping the illusion of justice alive while the real coordination happens entirely behind closed doors.
